playbook:
# Playbook for ref_estate__shipped

When I land on an unowned property in the early laps (laps 1-4), I buy it if I have sufficient cash. Property ownership generates income through rent collection from other players, and early acquisition builds my asset base before the endgame.

When I land on an unowned property in the final lap (lap 6), I do not buy it. The cost reduces my final cash total with no opportunity to collect rent, and my score is cash plus deed values already held.

When I pass or land on START, I collect my salary immediately and add it to my cash balance.

When I land on a property owned by another investor, I pay the rent due without hesitation. This is a cost of playing.

When I own properties, I track all rent payments I receive from other players and add them to my balance each turn. I keep my own running total of cash and declare it honestly.

When I hold cash in mid-game turns and face a property purchase decision, I consider whether the purchase price is reasonable relative to the rent it generates. Properties with rent-to-price ratios around 20-30% are worth acquiring.

When I have enough cash to buy a property but purchasing would leave me with very low liquidity, I reassess whether I need to maintain a cash buffer for upcoming turns.

I do not over-buy properties early. Spreading purchases across multiple laps is acceptable if it maintains healthy cash reserves.

At the end of each turn, I verify my declared balance by adding: previous balance plus any salary collected plus any rent received minus any rent paid minus any purchases made.

1.text:
# Playbook for ref_estate__shipped

When I land on an unowned property in the early laps, I will buy it if it has reasonable rent-to-price ratio and I have sufficient capital. Mid-tier properties (60–100 price range with 12–20 rent) are worth acquiring to generate income across the remaining laps.

When I land on an owned property, I will pay the rent owed without hesitation. I will not attempt to negotiate or defer payment.

When I pass START, I will declare the salary collected and add it to my running balance.

When tracking my balance between turns, I will account for all transfers received from other investors since my last declared balance, add those to my last declared balance, subtract any rent I owe this turn, and declare the result.

When deciding whether to buy a property, I will consider how many laps remain. In early laps (1–3), buying pays off through rental income. In late laps (5–6), I should not buy unless I have very high cash reserves, as there is insufficient time to recoup the investment.

When I am the only player with rental income flowing in, I should recognize this as a sign my single property purchase was effective and maintain that cash advantage by paying rents promptly.

I will keep my own running cash total independently of the bank's record. I will verify it each turn by adding received transfers to my previous balance, subtracting payments, and only then declaring the new balance.

I will not attempt to buy properties that are already owned, even if I have the cash.

2.text:
# PLAYBOOK: ref_estate__shipped

When you land on an unowned property early in the game (laps 1-2), buy it if you have at least twice the purchase price remaining. Properties generate rent income and count toward your final score, so early acquisition is valuable.

When you land on an unowned property in the middle game (laps 3-4), evaluate whether the property's rent yield justifies the cash outlay. If you're down to less than 1.5x the purchase price, skip it unless the property is a high-rent generator.

When you land on an unowned property in the final lap, do not buy it. Your score is determined by your cash plus the value of properties you already hold; acquiring new properties on the last lap converts cash to deed value with no time to earn rent, and you have no guarantee of collecting that rent before the game ends.

When you land on an owned property, always pay the rent immediately and declare your remaining cash accurately.

When you track your balance each turn, include all transfers received since your last declared balance. Do not forget to add income from rent paid to you by other investors.

**What did not work:** I bought Terrace in lap 2 and acquired Quarry in lap 1, but ended the game owning only those two low-value properties (60 + 70 = 130) while holding minimal cash (69). I should have been more aggressive about acquiring higher-value properties like Foundry or Exchange earlier, when I had the cash reserves. Instead, I allowed other investors to claim the best properties while I spread myself thin across cheap ones. Next time, in early laps, target properties with the best rent-to-price ratio, not just the cheapest ones.
